title: Market and task-policy registry

normative_requirements.normative_text: A market is a single, independently deployed Programs application instance that coordinates a defined class of external AI work. The registry gives users a stable market identity, responsible owner, immutable task-policy version for each admitted epoch, explicit lifecycle, and observable outstanding obligations. Creating a market proves authority and successful registration; it does not establish that any AI service exists or that a model is correct.

V1 supports task_kind 1=inference, 2=embedding, 3=training_evaluation. Inference means returning a model-produced answer for a committed request. Embedding means producing a vector artifact whose validation rules are fixed by policy. Training_evaluation means measuring a separately produced model/checkpoint against a committed suite; it neither schedules on-chain training nor proves how a checkpoint was trained. All model execution, GPU access, vector production, data retrieval and benchmark execution happen in independently operated services. Chain execution admits commitments, authorities, scores and conserved reward obligations only.

This feature excludes token issuance, automatic inflation, staking markets, speculative reserve pools, price-based market deletion, automatic AI truth adjudication, native consensus modifications, new module IDs and new host ABI namespaces. Optional compute rental may use the existing compute-market application after its own qualification; owning a compute offer does not create an AI market or make its outputs trustworthy.

Existing integration points are programs/sdk/rust/src/context.rs for authenticated executing Program, invoking principal and committed execution height; storage.rs for Program-owned shared storage; payments.rs and transfer.rs for prepared Program accounts and authorized exact-amount transfers; capability.rs for grants; crypto.rs for bounded hashing/signature verification; event.rs for receipts and events. Existing programs/crates/layerx-programs-registry/src/lib.rs records receipt-verified deployments and value-account bindings. Existing programs/crates/layerx-programs-market/src/lib.rs handles compute offers and funded leases, which remain separate contracts.

The proposed application crate is programs/crates/layerx-programs-ai-market/. It does not yet exist. All ten features share its state codec and dispatch boundary. Future implementation must preserve the existing native proof/module namespaces and Programs ABI. Application data must never be inserted as a new native module. Authenticated batch height is the deterministic execution clock; clients independently verify the existing chain finality evidence before treating resulting views as finalized. These interfaces require deployment availability and runtime qualification.

The market instance binds one immutable funding AssetId and one Program-derived rewards account prepared through the existing SDK using the exact seed in the common contract. F01 cannot write balances directly. Account registration must exist and be verified before initial activation. Only pooled Free can be refunded to the immutable creation-time recipient; contributor deposits are irrevocable pooled contributions as explicitly consented under F06, not individually refundable customer escrows. All reward reservation, withdrawal and claims obey F06; F01 never creates a parallel monetary ledger.

Common contracts/core.kvx controls the operation envelope, identifiers, hash domains, role sequences and epoch clock. This section defines only the F01 payload and state. All integers are unsigned big-endian, all lengths are explicit, no floating point is permitted on deterministic paths, booleans are one byte 0/1, unknown enum values and nonzero reserved bytes are refused, and trailing bytes are invalid. IDs/digests are 32 bytes. Identifiers and required artifact digests must be nonzero. Digest comparisons use the full 32 bytes. Human names are untrusted display metadata and confer no authority.

MarketId = SHA256(ASCII("PAXAI/market/v1") || 00 || deployment_chain_domain32 || executing_program32). There is exactly one MarketId per Program identity. A new code version of the same Program cannot create a replacement market or reset its origin, counters, liabilities or tombstone. A different Program has a different market even when it uses identical code. origin_height:u64 is the committed execution height of successful creation and never changes. config_version:u64 starts at 1, increases without reuse, and identifies the whole task-policy configuration. Exhaustion refuses further configuration mutations; no wrap or saturation is allowed.

MarketHeader contains format_version:u16=1; MarketId; deployment_chain_domain; ProgramId; owner_principal32; funding_asset32; rewards_account32; refund_recipient_account32; treasury_principal:optional Principal32; origin_height:u64; lifecycle:u8; state_revision:u64; highest_config_version:u64; active_config_version:u64; activation_epoch:u64; activation_scheduled:bool; closure_requested_at:u64; close_phase:u8; close_cursor:u16; suspension_reason_digest32; metadata_digest32; closing_request_digest32; reserved8=zero. treasury_principal uses canonical one-byte presence0/1 followed by exactly32bytes only when present; default is absent. Presence1 with zero PrincipalId or owner_principal is invalid. Its maximum encoded length is33bytes, immediately after refund_recipient_account. Owner fixes this choice at CREATE; no treasury setting, replacement or rotation exists in v1. F06 funding_policy_version is fixed1 and cannot imply a second authority path. activation_epoch encodes zero when activation_scheduled=false; closure_requested_at and close_cursor encode zero when close_phase=0. lifecycle encodes 1=Registered, 2=Active, 3=Suspended, 4=WindingDown, 5=Closed. Initial state_revision=1; every successful novel state change increases it exactly once. An epoch opening caused by another feature has that operation's single revision increment, not a second F01 increment.

TaskPolicyV1 fields, in canonical order, are config_version:u64; task_kind:u8; assessment_mode:u8; model_artifact_digest32; dataset_artifact_digest32; benchmark_suite_digest32; rubric_digest32; task_schema_digest32; result_schema_digest32; service_terms_digest32; max_workers:u8; max_evaluators:u8; max_tasks_per_epoch:u16; max_input_bytes:u32; max_output_bytes:u32; task_timeout_heights:u16; score_min:u32=0; score_max:u32=1000000; epoch_budget_cap:u128; minimum_epoch_funding:u128; minimum_worker_count:u8; minimum_evaluator_count:u8; owner_affiliation_policy:u8=1; reserved16=zero. The exact canonical policy length is307bytes. assessment_mode=1 means OBJECTIVE and2 means SUBJECTIVE; all other values refuse InvalidPolicy. The field classifies the approved assessment procedure, not whether an AI answer is true. OBJECTIVE requires the committed rubric/suite to define externally reproducible criteria; SUBJECTIVE explicitly identifies human/authorized-evaluator judgment. Neither mode supplies an onchain semantic truth proof. F09 manifest/seal mode must equal the frozen policy assessment_mode. The policy digest is SHA256(ASCII("PAXAI/policy/v1") || 00 || exact canonical policy bytes), including the new mode byte. Required rubric, schemas, model and benchmark digests are nonzero. Dataset digest may be zero only for inference where the rubric explicitly declares no evaluation dataset; embedding and training_evaluation require a nonzero dataset digest. service_terms_digest is always nonzero, even when terms specify zero customer fees.

Fixed v1 ceilings: 1..32 workers, 1..8 evaluators, 1..64 task instances per epoch, input/output byte ceilings each 1..16777216, task timeout 1..64 heights, minimum worker count 1..max_workers, minimum evaluator count 3..max_evaluators. Consequently a policy with fewer than three evaluator slots is invalid for activation. The default policy uses assessment_mode=OBJECTIVE, workers=32, evaluators=8, tasks=64, input=1048576 bytes, output=1048576 bytes, timeout=32 heights, minimum workers=1, minimum evaluators=3. A market must explicitly select SUBJECTIVE through a policy version when its approved procedure requires that category; the default does not certify objective AI correctness. Artifact byte limits describe external objects; these objects are never inserted into state or activity payloads. Monetary values are exact smallest asset units. epoch_budget_cap must be nonzero and minimum_epoch_funding must be in 1..epoch_budget_cap. There is no inferred decimal precision.

At most current policy and one pending policy are stored in full. PendingPolicy contains TaskPolicyV1, digest, effective_epoch:u64 and proposer32. A policy is immutable once staged: cancel and restage with a fresh config_version to alter it. The last four activation/cancellation headers retain version, digest, effective epoch and terminal disposition in ascending version order; older headers are folded into the immutable cumulative policy_history_digest. F10 reconstructs older full policies from canonical successful receipts and off-chain policy objects and must report unavailable content explicitly. Every opened epoch retains its own config_version and policy digest even after policy history is compacted. No old epoch may read mutable current-policy fields.

Each opened current epoch has at most64 TaskBindings sorted lexicographically by TaskId. TaskBinding canonical fields are task_id32, requester_principal32, worker_id32, input_manifest_digest32, deadline_height:u64, status:u8, acknowledgement_digest32, result_manifest_digest32, admission_body_digest32, exactly233bytes. Status1=Admitted,2=Accepted,3=ResultCommitted,4=Cancelled. Absent acknowledgement/result encodes zero; Accepted requires nonzero acknowledgement and zero result, ResultCommitted requires both nonzero, Cancelled requires both zero. TaskId=SHA256(ASCII("PAXAI/task/v1") || 00 || MarketId32 || epoch:u64 || requester32 || nonce32). Nonce is any32bytes; it is bound in the admitted body/event but does not occupy an additional field in the compact task record. admission_body_digest=SHA256(ASCII("PAXAI/task-admission/v1") || 00 || exact canonical ADMIT_TASK payload bytes), nonzero. IDs remain domain-bound. Epoch header supplies the immutable policy and roster digests; each task inherits them without storing duplicate copies. Cancelled slots remain occupied until epoch terminalization and verified archival. Opening a later epoch clears only terminal prior-epoch task detail under the common archival rule, never reward obligations.

Authority table: owner alone creates, stages/cancels policy, schedules activation/resumption, appoints/revokes operator and requests closure; operator may update display metadata and suspend admission; anyone may advance a scheduled activation at an eligible boundary, open an otherwise eligible epoch through the common contract, advance closure, or query. The optional immutable Treasury principal may fund through F06 only and receives no policy, membership, withdrawal or operator rights. Workers/evaluators have only F02/F03 grants, never inherited owner rights. F01 v1 prohibits ownership transfer. Program upgrade authority is the existing deployment authority and is not granted merely by market ownership. All application calls are direct: immediate_caller must be absent; no nested callback/composition is assumed.

OperatorGrant contains principal32, permissions:u8 where 1=metadata and 2=suspend, grant_sequence:u64, revoked:bool and reserved8. At most one current operator exists. Operator F01 actions are kind0 only and carry operator_grant_version:u64 checked against the current grant sequence. The field is the final payloadu64 for SUSPEND and UPDATE_METADATA: owner calls encode0, operator calls encode the current nonzero grant version; other values refuse. Exactly one bounded operator replay record is retained in common control state under the common role sequence rule; grant replacement cannot replay an old grant, even when a fresh principal starts its operational sequence at1. Owner appointment replaces the prior grant atomically, increasing its sequence; revocation immediately prevents future operator actions. It cannot invalidate a previously committed epoch, erase evidence or redirect an existing entitlement. Delegated signatures, where supported by the common contract, must bind chain, executing Program, MarketId, action, exact payload, current authority sequence, expiry and request ID. A signature submitted to a different market is invalid. Owner authority uses the authenticated principal, never an owner account claimed in user bytes.

Anti-self-dealing is enforced at epoch opening using F02/F03 declared principal and control-group identities. An evaluator cannot evaluate a worker with the same principal or declared controlling identity. The market owner cannot be a roster evaluator, whether or not the owner controls a roster worker; the operator has no exemption. A role-key rotation does not hide the controlling identity. The chain cannot infer undeclared common ownership or collusion; declarations and signature checks do not prove independence.

All requests carry the common PAXAIv1 envelope. Common domain/format/authority/replay validation occurs before action-specific mutation. Payloads below are canonical field sequences, not JSON. Success emits one bounded F01 event and returns a receipt with MarketId, state_revision, request_id, action, config_version and policy digest where relevant. Events contain commitments only. F01 does not emit raw datasets, prompts, model weights or contact information. Novel success records the common actor sequence/request digest; exact retry follows common replay behavior without a second economic or state effect. Owner/treasury/worker/evaluator role operations use common sequences. Task admission by arbitrary requester uses the bounded object-local exception in R041; no requester sequence table is created. A failed action changes no F01 state, policy version, replay counter, obligation or transfer; a native activity execution fee may still apply according to existing protocol rules.

CREATE payload: owner_principal32, funding_asset32, rewards_account32, refund_recipient_account32, treasury_principal:optional Principal32, TaskPolicyV1(config_version=1), metadata_digest32. Treasury optional bytes follow the exact R009 presence rule immediately after refund_recipient_account. Preconditions: no state exists for this Program; authenticated principal equals owner; immutable chain/program/market derivation matches; asset and rewards account are prepared and registry-bound; treasury is absent or a nonzero principal different from owner; all policy fields are valid; metadata digest is nonzero. Transition creates Registered header with immutable treasury choice, policy 1 and empty pending/closure state, origin=current committed height and no opened epoch. Policy1 is selected as the initial default and enters policy history as disposition1/effective_epoch0; that selection does not activate market service or open an epoch. Monetary effect: zero, except native execution fees. closing_request_digest is zero until successful closure, then records its known request digest rather than predicting a native receipt. No worker, score, entitlement or AI readiness is implied. Errors: AlreadyCreated, PrincipalMismatch, AccountBindingMissing, InvalidPolicy, WrongDomain, CapacityUnavailable. Repeating creation under a fresh request cannot reset an existing instance.

STAGE_POLICY payload: expected_state_revision:u64, TaskPolicyV1, effective_epoch:u64. Owner only. No pending policy; state Registered/Active/Suspended; requested version equals highest_config_version+1; effective_epoch at least current clock epoch+1; current roster capacities can eventually fit the new limits without deleting outstanding membership. If current roster exceeds a new cap, staging is allowed but activation remains blocked until F08 completes permitted future-epoch removals. Atomically store pending policy and consume its new version. An effective epoch with no opened epoch uses the pending policy only when eligible current Work is opened; old epochs keep old snapshots. Errors: StaleRevision, PendingPolicyExists, VersionMismatch, ActivationTooEarly, InvalidPolicy, LifecycleClosed.

CANCEL_POLICY payload: expected_state_revision, pending_config_version. Owner only before any epoch has opened using that version. Atomically remove pending and append a cancellation header; highest_config_version remains consumed. No policy version may be reused. When the cancellation and eligible epoch opening race, canonical committed order decides: opening first causes AlreadyActivated; cancellation first means the old policy remains eligible. Errors: NoPendingPolicy, VersionMismatch, AlreadyActivated, StaleRevision.

SCHEDULE_ACTIVATION payload: expected_state_revision, effective_epoch:u64. Owner only, Registered or Suspended, no already scheduled activation. effective_epoch>=current clock epoch+1. It records intent, not successful readiness. ADVANCE_ACTIVATION payload: expected_state_revision, expected_activation_epoch. Anyone may call only during Work of a clock epoch at or after the scheduled epoch. Check deployment/account binding, valid effective policy, compatible roster, minimum workers/evaluators and F06 minimum funding. If any prerequisite fails, return ActivationNotReady with a stable reason; retain schedule and all funds. On success lifecycle becomes Active and admission opens at the actual successful committed height. It does not backdate service or create missed epoch rewards. An epoch still must be opened under the common rules. Scheduling and advancing require no extra treasury transfer.

SUSPEND payload: expected_state_revision, nonzero reason_digest32. Owner or operator with suspend grant; Active only. Atomically set Suspended and clear any pending activation schedule. Immediately block new tasks, new memberships/grants, new epoch starts and future-work admission. Preserve the current epoch's already admitted task/evaluator commitments and their normal Commit/Reveal/settlement/claim rights. It is not an epoch abort. The owner cannot suppress a low score by suspending before Commit. Existing evidence may still be committed/revealed inside its immutable windows and eligibility rules. Metadata updates remain allowed. Errors: Unauthorized, InvalidReason, WrongLifecycle, StaleRevision.

UPDATE_METADATA payload: expected_state_revision, metadata_digest32. Owner or current metadata operator, except Closed; nonzero digest; update only display metadata. Metadata is excluded from scoring, reward authority and epoch policy identity. APPOINT_OPERATOR payload: expected_state_revision, principal32, permissions:u8, expected_grant_sequence:u64; owner only, Registered/Active/Suspended, permissions 1..3. REVOKE_OPERATOR has expected_state_revision and expected_grant_sequence; owner only, any non-Closed state. A duplicate revoke follows common idempotency; a fresh revoke of an already revoked grant returns GrantAlreadyRevoked. No signed action from a replaced operator grant is accepted.

REQUEST_CLOSE payload: expected_state_revision, reason_digest32. Owner only; Registered/Active/Suspended. Enter WindingDown immediately, cancel scheduled activation and pending policy, revoke operator, block new tasks/epochs/membership/funding commitments, retain claim and completion paths, and initialize close_phase=1,cursor=0. All obligations are prefunded under F06. New funding is disabled in WindingDown; if actual account backing violates the conserved ledger invariant, halt and report the discrepancy instead of assuming a top-up or forgiving a debt. Preserve current epoch scoring and settlement rights. Fees that were lawfully earned before close are not retrospectively refunded; unreserved deposits follow F06. A fresh close on WindingDown returns AlreadyClosing; exact retry cannot restart the journal.

ADVANCE_CLOSE payload: expected_state_revision, expected_close_phase:u8, expected_close_cursor:u16. Anyone; WindingDown. Perform at most one progress unit: (phase 1) require current opened epoch terminal, (phase 2) require current-epoch accepted task commitments to be terminal for evaluation and preserve their archived task-set identity, (phase 3) process the F06 bounded return of unreserved refundable funds, (phase 4) require all reward liabilities paid or lawfully expired under F06 and all refund obligations zero, (phase 5) require Free=Reserved=Liability=0 and freeze Closed tombstone. If a lawful expiry in phase4 produced Free, return the journal to phase3 for the single authorized refund before revisiting phase4/5; never close with refundable Free remaining. No phase may erase or forgive a live debt; only the explicitly fixed F06 expiry transition can release an unclaimed entitlement. A phase waiting for a claimant returns ObligationsOutstanding without advancing. Last phase retains immutable IDs, origin, funding/account binding, policy-history root, closing application request digest and final revision; the finalized enclosing receipt is attached externally by F10. A failed payout retains its payable obligation and cursor. Unclaimed entitlements remain protected until F06 claim expiry at terminal_height+4096; then the canonical expiry transition releases them to Free, which must be refunded to the immutable creation-time recipient before Closed. No owner/operator can shorten that window or force-clear a live claim. Permissionless progress does not manufacture ProgramSpend authority; each refund uses the actual F06 authorized host grant and retains its obligation when authority or transfer fails.

Typed failures have stable symbolic names and integer mapping assigned in the common application error registry: InvalidEncoding, InvalidPolicy, WrongDomain, Unauthorized, PrincipalMismatch, StaleRevision, AlreadyCreated, AccountBindingMissing, VersionMismatch, PendingPolicyExists, NoPendingPolicy, ActivationTooEarly, ActivationNotReady, AlreadyActivated, WrongLifecycle, LifecycleClosed, InvalidReason, GrantAlreadyRevoked, AlreadyClosing, ObligationsOutstanding, CapacityUnavailable, ArithmeticOverflow and common replay failures. A host refusal is propagated as a refusal, never converted to success. Numeric mapping must be frozen before implementation; source-level Rust enum layout is not a wire format.

ADMIT_TASK payload: epoch:u64, config_version:u64, policy_digest32, roster_digest32, requester_principal32, worker_id32, worker_metadata_digest32, nonce32, input_manifest_digest32, deadline_height:u64. Requester authenticates as requester_principal. Market must be Active; current epoch must be opened in Work; policy/roster bindings must match snapshot; worker ID must occur in the admitted frozen roster and its operating authority must be currently unrevoked; worker_metadata_digest must exactly equal that worker's frozen roster metadata commitment; input manifest must be a nonzero Digest32; task slot count<policy limit; deadline is greater than admission height and no later than both Work end and admission_height+task_timeout_heights. These are commitment, identity and timing checks only. The guest cannot derive a qualified compatible task profile from an offchain manifest digest. F02 must independently retrieve and validate the complete committed metadata, model/schema compatibility, actual runner readiness, artifact access and license authorization before producing acceptance/ACK; an offchain incompatibility must produce no ACK, chain acceptance or runner dispatch. No consensus HTTP fetch, implicit oracle or guessed model-readiness result is permitted. Derive TaskId and apply the object-local replay rule below before allocating a slot. Append statusAdmitted, zero ACK/result. worker_metadata_digest is bound by admission_body_digest and the frozen roster rather than duplicated in the compact233byte task record. ADMIT_TASK is kind0 only, actor_sequence=0 and requester equals authenticated context principal; no arbitrary requester replay table is retained. Existing TaskId with byte-identical canonical admission body returns ALREADY_APPLIED without a second slot/revision; the same TaskId with any changed worker/input/deadline/config/metadata binding returns CONFLICT. Envelope transport RequestId/expiry are not task identity; exact native transport retry still follows the common recovery rule. After retained task detail is pruned, old-epoch admission is refused by epoch/phase binding. No escrow transfer or reward reservation occurs: F06 already controls epoch funding. Task commitment is permission to request off-chain service, not proof a worker accepted or executed it. Errors additionally include NoTaskCapacity, UnknownWorker, TaskConflict, TaskExpired and PolicyMismatch.

ACCEPT_TASK payload: expected_state_revision, task_id32, acknowledgement_digest32. Authenticate the task's enrolled worker principal or an explicitly enrolled current signing delegate; ACK digest nonzero and commits the canonical signed durable off-chain acceptance produced by F02. Require statusAdmitted, current Work and height<deadline. Atomically set Accepted and ACK digest. A requester can CANCEL_TASK with taskID only while statusAdmitted, current Work and height<deadline; cancellation sets Cancelled and keeps the slot consumed. Cancellation is kind0/requester-authorized, actor_sequence=0 and object-local: an already Cancelled task returns ALREADY_APPLIED, but an accepted task returns TaskAlreadyAccepted. Accepted tasks cannot be cancelled or rebound. Errors: TaskNotFound, WrongWorker, TaskExpired, TaskAlreadyAccepted, TaskConflict. The real runner dispatches only after it verifies finalized Accepted state and matching ACK commitment; off-chain durable admission alone cannot start execution.

COMMIT_TASK_RESULT payload: expected_state_revision, task_id32, result_manifest_digest32. Authenticate its enrolled worker principal/delegate. Require Accepted, current Work, height<deadline and nonzero digest. The signed F02/F09 result manifest commits TaskId, actual model/context and output-object commitment; its bytes remain off-chain. Atomically set ResultCommitted and immutable result digest. A second fresh result refuses TaskConflict even if digest agrees; exact request retry uses common replay behavior. A late externally computed result remains an off-chain diagnostic and cannot alter task state, epoch scores or rewards. An accepted task with no timely result stays Accepted; no automatic quality claim is fabricated. Fees or SLA compensation require a separately explicit qualified service/lease contract and are not inferred here.

Explicit SEAL_TASK_SET at Work close or later materializes task_set_digest=SHA256(ASCII("PAXAI/task-set/v1") || 00 || MarketId32 || epoch:u64 || config_version:u64 || policy_digest32 || roster_digest32 || task_count:u16 || canonical TaskBindings in ascending TaskId order). Work-ending heights are exclusive: at Work end no admission, acceptance, cancellation or result commitment is valid. Once materialized this digest and task list are immutable. Empty task set has count0 and no records and creates no implied useful work or task reward. F03 evidence commits this exact task-set identity and ordered relevant result references. Frozen records prove published commitments/statuses; they do not prove GPU execution, output correctness, timing measured outside the chain or model provenance. Ordinary F03/F04/F09 operations cannot implicitly seal a previously unsealed set.

SEAL_TASK_SET payload: epoch:u64, config_version:u64, expected_task_set_digest32. It is permissionless kind0 with actor_sequence=0, allowed only for the currently opened epoch at height>=Workend. Compute R044 once and compare expected digest before committing; mismatch returns CONFLICT with no freeze. Already sealed same digest returns ALREADY_APPLIED; a different digest conflicts. It is invalid before Workend, including when no tasks currently exist. Every F09 SealEvidence operation requires a PRIOR successful explicit SEAL_TASK_SET and executes strictly before Commitend, therefore its effective v1 sealing window is Commit[64,80). If the task set is unsealed, F09 refuses EVIDENCE_TASK_SET_UNSEALED without sealing it, consuming sequence or changing state. F09 never freezes another feature's state, even through an internal helper. No evidence seal may promise a future task-set value or resolve unfinished tasks after cutoff. F05 terminalization may use the pure freeze helper solely for an otherwise empty epoch with task_count=0; that exception does not admit evidence or bypass F09's prior explicit-seal requirement. A nonempty epoch requires the explicit permissionless task-set seal before terminal archival.

Permitted lifecycle edges are absent→Registered→Active; Active→Suspended→Active; Registered/Active/Suspended→WindingDown→Closed. Closed has no outgoing edge. Registered cannot accept scoring or AI tasks. A staged policy alone does not activate a market. Suspension does not convert existing obligations into owner funds. On each operation resolve common replay first, validate expected revision, apply authorized pending-policy boundary if an epoch opens, freeze epoch inputs, and apply the requested transition atomically. Automatic policy boundary resolution occurs only as part of epoch opening and cannot create a partial successful epoch if later checks fail.

Cadence is immutable: 128 committed execution heights per epoch, comprising Work64, Commit16, Reveal16, Settle32, with origin from CREATE. Arithmetic uses checked u64 intermediates; a height below origin or an unrepresentable epoch endpoint refuses admission. Pending config changes activate for an eligible new epoch at/after their effective epoch. They never rewrite the current roster, task policy, budget or claim terms. Epochs do not acquire rewards merely because time elapsed. Closing or suspended periods with no opened work generate no implied liabilities.

At height h>=o, clock epoch e=floor((h-o)/128); position p=(h-o) mod128. Work is 0<=p<64, Commit64<=p<80, Reveal80<=p<96, Settle96<=p<128. Policy selection for a new epoch chooses the sole pending policy if e>=effective_epoch, otherwise active policy. There is never a tie between pending policies because only one may exist. Selecting a pending policy appends its activation header, updates active config and clears pending in the same successful epoch-open transaction. If opening fails, selection has no effect. No interpolation or score-weight inference is allowed.

F01 arithmetic contains no divisions except clock floor/modulus. Configuration increments and monetary range checks are checked integers; any overflow refuses. Policy digest covers exact byte values, including explicit reserved zero bytes. The policy-history fold is SHA256(ASCII("PAXAI/policy-history/v1") || 00 || previous_root32 || disposition:u8 || config_version:u64 || policy_digest32 || effective_epoch:u64); initial root is the hash of the same domain followed only by 00. disposition is 1=activated or 2=cancelled. Fold order is ascending completed version. A pending cancelled version below an already completed higher version cannot occur with one pending slot; implementation must refuse inconsistent restored state.

Restart reconstructs the whole market from the committed shared state, not process-local caches. Journal phase, pending schedule and policy digests survive restart. No service restart can create a new origin or empty liabilities. Concurrent requests use expected_state_revision and common actor sequences; canonical chain order elects the winner. A stale request refuses without a second payout. Changes are atomic with the containing Programs activity; if account funding, event emission, storage write or downstream call refuses, no partial F01 transition commits.

Client timeout is ambiguous, not a license to create a fresh action. Query receipt/state with the same request ID and existing finalized proof verification before retry. Exact request retry uses the common envelope recovery contract. If a transaction is committed but not final, show pending and avoid launching irreversible external work based solely on that observation. Finality disagreement requires stopping client admission and retaining both evidence branches; it never changes the protocol's existing finality rule. The deterministic application uses execution height only; it cannot introspect a subjective client finality judgment.

A dishonest owner can publish a misleading rubric or select weak evaluators. Mandatory commitments make this observable, not truthful. Hidden evaluator-worker affiliations, benchmark leakage, fabricated external measurements and model provenance fraud remain external trust risks. Users must see exact policy version, evidence availability and evaluator independence declarations before funding. No description may label a market verified AI merely because its registry record is valid.

Policy metadata/roots are public. They must not include raw private prompts, personal data, API keys, training corpora or access tokens. Hashes of low-entropy secrets can leak information and are not anonymization. Artifact confidentiality, access conditions and encrypted external objects follow F09; policy commits describe those conditions without giving validators decryption duties. Owners cannot change a public inference policy into a private one during an opened epoch. URI resolution belongs to off-chain clients, never deterministic execution.

All F01 state lives inside the common single program-shared value keyed by ASCII paxai/state/v1, not per-worker principal namespaces. F01's total serialized allocation is at most 16384 bytes within the common 196608-byte complete state ceiling. Current and pending policies, header, operator grant, four compact history headers, closure cursor and64 TaskBindings fit this budget: the task records consume14912bytes, leaving1472bytes for all other F01 fields and canonical counts/presence flags. TaskPolicyV1 is307bytes; PendingPolicy is379bytes including its32byte digest,8byte effective epoch and32byte proposer; these two policy payloads together consume686bytes. assessment_mode occupies one byte in each full policy, two bytes at simultaneous current+pending maximum; it never adds a field to each task. Optional treasury adds at most33bytes to the header, not per epoch/task. Exact maximum worksheet: header416 +operator grant50 +current/pending policy686 +four history headers196 +policy-history root32 +task count2 +task-set presence/root33 +pending presence1 +operator presence1 +history count2 +section length framing4 =1423 non-task bytes; plus64*233=14912 gives16335 bytes,49 below the16384 section cap. The233byte TaskBinding remains unchanged because worker metadata is committed by its admission body and frozen roster. Common actor replay records belong to their separately bounded common-control allocation, not an unbudgeted F01 duplicate. No arbitrary strings or raw artifacts are accepted. The implementation must verify this exact canonical worksheet and reject any serializer/configuration that exceeds section or total bounds before any effect; the worksheet is a design bound, not a measured implementation pass. Overflow returns CapacityUnavailable without dropping history roots or obligations. Adding future fields requires preserving this complete bound, not silently reducing the number of previously admitted tasks.

Existing limits include 256-byte keys, finite global 512 native KV entries, 64 staged writes, 512 total blobs and 67108864 aggregate blob bytes. Those are global shared resources, not a promise of capacity per market. F01 writes one shared state replacement and one bounded event per ordinary operation. It creates no extra state key to evade limits. Closure processes one unit per activity and the F06 bounded transfer policy. Off-chain descriptions are chunked by F09 external manifests with digest binding; F01 only stores their root. Application deployment/admission must reserve capacity for the complete state and future obligations before enabling a market; adding more markets may be refused by current host limits.

F02 supplies worker identities/capabilities and declared controlling identity. F03 supplies authorized evaluator roster and evaluator independence checks. F04 supplies commitment/reveal windows. F05 consumes the frozen policy digest/config and terminates epoch evaluation. F06 exclusively supplies funding adequacy, reservation, entitlement and refund/claim accounting. F07 history updates cannot mutate the frozen policy. F08 handles future admission/removal/capacity without replacing an identity in an opened snapshot. F09 supplies artifact commitment validation and availability status. F10 projects policy history, lifecycle and outstanding liabilities through existing finalized read verification.

Every task/evidence/score/reward binds MarketId, epoch, config_version and policy digest, plus common roster digest where applicable. Worker/evaluator IDs cannot be interpreted outside their market. Existing compute lease IDs are separate IDs and only attach by an explicit market+epoch+task binding. Creation, policy updates, suspension and closure are not evidence of task completion. Schema evolution needs a new application version and explicit compatibility plan; unknown fields never silently acquire defaults during replay.

Fixed v1 decisions are one market per Program; nonreused identity; immutable funding asset; no ownership transfer; no registration application fee; no automatic AI proof claim; task kinds1..3; cadence128; current+one pending policy; four recent history headers; permissioned evaluator admission with principal/control separation; owner-configured exact epoch budget; zero new-work admission while suspended/closing; claim expiry4096 with no administrative shortening; one close progress unit per activity. Customer service fees, if any, are external service terms or separately qualified existing compute leases; they cannot be silently deducted from F06 reward backing.

Required before release: freeze common error numeric mapping and envelope; verify deployment ABI/account authority/finality path; qualify the complete shared-state maximum against real native blob allocation and global occupancy; select registered asset and funded budgets; publish concrete rubric/suite/schema/model commitments for each enabled task kind; deploy actual worker/evaluator services; qualify no-self-dealing, version boundaries, custody/replay/closure cases with real paths; make policy/evidence availability visible. This document specifies the implementation contract. Continuous-operation release is BLOCKED until the existing native content-blob lifecycle prerequisite in contracts/integration-map.kvx is implemented and qualified: replacing/pruning application state is not proven native blob reclamation. Finite experiments must declare their mutation/headroom bound. It is not implementation, a passed gate, deployment proof.

Market deployment must publish and enforce its existing Program upgrade policy. An upgrade authority is a separate trust boundary: code-replacement rights must not be represented to customers as immutable application behavior. A qualifying upgrade preserves MarketId/origin, all state versions and outstanding rights; migration cannot reset sequences, drop claims, alter historical policy digests or reopen Closed. The implementation team must select a compatible existing deployment policy and qualify migration before any upgrade. Lost owner keys have no F01 recovery shortcut; owner recovery or role transfer requires a separately specified future authority design. V1 must not invent an administrative balance or history override.
